plants.name: Prunus yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous tree that produces masses of delicate, fragrant, five-petaled flowers before its leaves emerge, creating clouds of blossom. It is the iconic cherry of Japanese hanami celebrations and widely planted in temperate parks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid April in Japan; early to mid March in warmer parts of its range such as Kyushu and southern regions
plants.location: Japan (Kyushu and southern Honshu), also cultivated in Washington D.C., Korea, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The cherry trees around the Tidal Basin in Washington D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and their bloom forecast is watched closely each spring.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with a trumpet-shaped central corona surrounded by six petal-like tepals. It carpets woodlands and meadows and is the parent of many garden daffodil varieties.
plants.location: Western Europe, including England, Wales, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain lycorine and galantamine; galantamine is extracted from related Amaryllidaceae plants to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A large Himalayan tree that bears huge, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches in late winter and early spring. Individual blossoms can reach 25 cm across and are strikingly showy.
plants.location: Himalayan foothills (Nepal, Bhutan, northeast India, southwest China); cultivated in mild temperate gardens in the UK, New Zealand, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, and their flowers evolved before bees existed, so they are pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: An evergreen shrub producing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl-shaped crown of silky pink-tipped bracts surrounding a center of tiny true flowers. It is adapted to fire-prone fynbos habitats.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through early winter, with peak flowering in autumn in the Southern Hemisphere; some blooms appear in March
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape of South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its heads can reach up to 30 cm in diameter.
